title: Tutoring Center Story Sprint Pack - Middle Sprint Lane

sprints.title: Acorn Avenue Errand Order Sprint
sprints.sessionFit: 12-minute warmup for one-to-one or pair tutoring.
sprints.tutorSetup: Print one page, choose three errand slips, and set a pencil beside the route box.
sprints.kidDirection: Sort the acorn errands, add one exact detail for each stop, and draft the helper note.
sprints.coachingPrompt: Ask which stop must happen first, then have the writer point to the detail that proves it.

pageSections.heading: Errand Clues
lines: The first leaf slip asks for ____________________.
The second leaf slip belongs near ____________________.
The third leaf slip gives the clue ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Short Draft
lines: My middle sentence adds the detail ____________________.

sprints.wrapUpLine: One sequence word I used well is ____________________.
sprints.extensionLine: Add a fourth stop that changes the route by ____________________.

sprints.title: Button Bakery Clear Map Sprint
sprints.sprintSkill: Map clues, exact nouns, and clear order
sprints.sessionFit: 10-minute table warmup before a longer writing turn.
sprints.tutorSetup: Draw a quick bakery path with three turns, then hand the writer the fill-in page.
sprints.kidDirection: Fix the bakery map by choosing clear clues, ordering the turns, and writing a tidy route draft.
sprints.coachingPrompt: Ask the writer to replace one vague word with a thing readers can picture.

pageSections.heading: Map Draft
lines: The map mixup is fixed when ____________________.

sprints.wrapUpLine: The exact noun that helped my map is ____________________.
sprints.extensionLine: Add one new bakery clue that points to ____________________.

sprints.title: Rain Gauge Railway Log Sprint
sprints.sprintSkill: Observation details, cause, and next step
sprints.sessionFit: 15-minute tutoring warmup for detail work and short explanatory drafting.
sprints.tutorSetup: Set out the page, mark three imaginary gauge levels, and invite the writer to choose one route.
sprints.kidDirection: Read the gauge clue, choose the railway stops, and draft a log that explains the route.
sprints.coachingPrompt: Ask what changed, why it matters, and which detail should appear before the next step.

pageSections.heading: Route Cause
lines: The switch changes the route near ____________________.
The next stop needs a note about ____________________.

sprints.wrapUpLine: One cause-and-effect phrase I used is ____________________.
sprints.extensionLine: Add a second gauge clue that changes the next stop to ____________________.

sprints.title: Rain Boot Route Sequence Sprint
sprints.sessionFit: 10-minute quick start for a hesitant writer or small pair.
sprints.tutorSetup: Circle three route spots on the page and model one transition word aloud.
sprints.kidDirection: Choose a boot route, add dry path details, and write the ranger message in order.
sprints.coachingPrompt: Ask the writer to say the route aloud once, then write the words in the same order.

pageSections.heading: Ranger Draft
lines: My second sentence adds the detail ____________________.
My last sentence gives the message ____________________.

sprints.wrapUpLine: The transition word that made my route clearer is ____________________.
sprints.extensionLine: Add one route sign that warns the ranger to check ____________________.

sprints.title: Pocket Park Notice Detail Sprint
sprints.sprintSkill: Specific details and short notice drafting
sprints.sessionFit: 12-minute tutoring page for detail practice before independent writing.
sprints.tutorSetup: Offer three tiny notice choices and have the writer underline the clearest one.
sprints.kidDirection: Pick one park notice, add exact park details, and draft the helper's next message.
sprints.coachingPrompt: Ask which detail readers need first so the helper knows what to do.

pageSections.heading: Notice Choice
lines: The missing detail on the notice is ____________________.

sprints.wrapUpLine: The detail that made my notice clearer is ____________________.
sprints.extensionLine: Write a second notice that asks for ____________________.

sprints.title: Penny Path Direction Draft Sprint
sprints.sprintSkill: Direction words, clue order, and concise drafting
sprints.sessionFit: 10-minute warmup for direction language and sentence order.
sprints.tutorSetup: Point to the compass shop, mark two path turns, and ask the writer to choose the final stop.
sprints.kidDirection: Follow the button compass, order the clues, and write a short direction draft.
sprints.coachingPrompt: Ask the writer to test the route by tracing each turn with a finger before drafting.
sprints.wrapUpLine: The direction word I used clearly is ____________________.
sprints.extensionLine: Add a new compass clue that leads to ____________________.

sprints.title: Seed Library Map Note Sprint
sprints.sprintSkill: Observation notes, sequence, and concise revision
sprints.sessionFit: 15-minute tutoring sprint for short draft planning and revision.
sprints.tutorSetup: Set the map page beside a pencil, then ask the writer to choose one seed drawer and one route.
sprints.kidDirection: Choose a seed drawer, map the route, and draft a return note with exact observations.
sprints.coachingPrompt: Ask the writer to keep the best observation and remove one extra word before the final line.

pageSections.heading: Return Note
lines: One word I can remove is ____________________.

sprints.wrapUpLine: The observation I kept in my final note is ____________________.
sprints.extensionLine: Add a second seed drawer that changes the route by ____________________.
